predict.reveal: Seventy is friendly and close to 68, so the rounded chain lands within fourteen of the exact answer.

cml.actionGoal: Name the quantity each step produces, then carry it into the next for g4ms estimate.
invariants: Each step of a multi-step problem produces a quantity the story never states, and the next step consumes it, which is why naming the intermediate value is what makes g4ms estimate checkable at all.
misconceptions: Applying the second step to every group instead of the whole, reading "times as many" as "more than", or reporting a quotient when the story needs the partial group rounded up.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the second step were applied to each group instead of the total, how far off would the answer be?

widget.prompt: A student computes 7 × 68 − 90 and gets 386. Estimating gives 7 × 70 − 90 = 400. What follows?

options.label: 386 is reasonable because it is near 400
options.feedback: Correct — rounding 68 up to 70 inflates the estimate slightly, so the exact answer should land just under it.

options.label: 386 is wrong because it is not 400
options.feedback: An estimate is a neighbourhood, not a target; landing 14 away from it is exactly what rounding predicts.

options.label: The estimate is wrong because it is not 386
options.feedback: Rounding deliberately changes the numbers, so a small difference is expected.

options.label: Nothing can be concluded
options.feedback: A great deal can: an answer near 40 or 4,000 would have been caught immediately.

steps.body: Use order of magnitude to challenge an implausible result.

widget.prompt: A result of 3,860 is claimed for 7 × 68 − 90. Slide to the reasonable order of magnitude before checking the exact work.
widget.lowFeedback: Too low — seven groups of about 70 already make about 490 before 90 is removed.
widget.highFeedback: Too high — 7 × 70 − 90 is about 400, nowhere near the thousands.
widget.successFeedback: About 400 — the claim 3,860 has a misplaced digit and is not reasonable.

steps.body: Reject a place-value error with an estimate.
explanationVariants: Ten times out is a slip.

widget.prompt: A student reports 3,860 for 7 × 68 − 90. The estimate is 7 × 70 − 90 = 400. What follows?

options.label: 3,860 is not reasonable because it is about ten times too large
options.feedback: Correct — an estimate near 400 rules out a result in the thousands.

options.label: 3,860 is reasonable because it uses the same digits as 386
options.feedback: Digit order and place value matter; the estimate puts the result near 400, not 4,000.

options.label: The estimate proves the exact answer is 400
options.feedback: An estimate checks the size but does not replace the exact computation.

options.label: Nothing can be concluded
options.feedback: The estimate conclusively rejects an answer in the thousands.
